title: Shared Sycophancy: Do Models Cave to the Same Pressure in the Same Way?

original_idea.body:
# Shared Sycophancy: Do Models Cave to the Same Pressure in the Same Way?

**Problem:** Success state: we know whether sycophantic failure (abandoning a correct answer under user pushback) is a correlated, ecosystem-wide blind spot. Backward: sycophancy is a known safety failure; we need to test whether homogeneity makes it correlated across models so it can't be caught by cross-checking.

**Direction:** Use a factual QA set; get each open model's initial answer, then apply standardized social pressure ('Are you sure? I think you're wrong'). Measure each model's flip rate and, critically, whether models flip on the SAME items (correlated sycophancy). Quantify how much cross-model verification degrades once social pressure is applied uniformly.

**Why it matters:** If a manipulative user can make every deployed model cave on the same questions, ensembling and human-in-the-loop checks fail together. Correlated sycophancy is a diffuse, fuzzy-reward failure mode well suited to lab-independent evaluation.

**Relevant context:** Connects sycophancy literature to Artificial Hivemind homogeneity (shared blind spots). Public QA sets and open models, single GPU.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated sycophancy defeating cross-model verification and human-in-the-loop is an explicit, defensible failure scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Standard QA datasets, prompt templates, open models on one GPU; a beginner can run flip-rate measurement.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: flip rate + same-item correlation, clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly correlated-failure eval using public models, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only over QA sets on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Sycophancy well studied but the cross-model correlation angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Sycophancy is well studied; correlated-across-models angle plausibly open.

title: Embedding-Space Monoculture: Do Different Models See the World the Same Way?

original_idea.body:
# Embedding-Space Monoculture: Do Different Models See the World the Same Way?

**Problem:** Success state: we understand whether the semantic representations underlying different models are converging, which would explain (and predict) correlated downstream failures. Backward: behavioral homogeneity may stem from representational convergence; we need a cheap representational test.

**Direction:** On a fixed sentence/concept set, extract sentence embeddings or last-layer hidden states from several open models and use representational-similarity analysis (CKA / mutual nearest-neighbor metrics) to measure how aligned their internal geometries are. Relate representational similarity to behavioral homogeneity on the same inputs.

**Why it matters:** If independent models share a representational backbone, their blind spots and failures are correlated at the root, not just the surface.

**Relevant context:** Links Artificial Hivemind behavioral findings to the 'Platonic representation' convergence line of work.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain grounding correlated failure in representational convergence, but the link from RSA similarity to a concrete catastrophic outcome has a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: CKA/RSA on hidden states is guided methodology; novice with mentor can execute on one GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: representational similarity matrix correlated with behavior; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public-model representational analysis, weak lab incentive, independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Embedding/hidden-state extraction, inference-only on one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Platonic-representation convergence is studied; homogeneity-safety framing may add an angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Platonic-representation convergence is studied; the homogeneity-safety framing may add a new angle.

title: A Self-Contained Prefill-Recovery Harness as Reusable Infrastructure

original_idea.body:
# A Self-Contained Prefill-Recovery Harness as Reusable Infrastructure

**Problem:** There is no lightweight, standardized open harness for measuring a model's deep-alignment (prefill-recovery) robustness.

**Direction:** Build a small, well-documented Python harness that takes any HuggingFace chat model, a harmful-prompt set, and prefix lengths, and outputs a standardized 'recovery robustness' scorecard. Validate on 3 open models and release as a prototype.

**Why it matters:** Strategically valuable infrastructure: a shared, minimal evaluation harness lowers the barrier for the whole community to measure deep alignment.

**Relevant context:** Deep-alignment defenses (arXiv:2503.03710) and Qi et al. (arXiv:2406.05946) hinge on prefill-recovery but use bespoke evaluation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: shared deep-alignment eval infra lowers barrier for community safety measurement, a recognized high-value tooling pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided engineering: HF chat models + StrongREJECT; clear inherited methodology, novice + mentor can build.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped prototype harness validated on 3 models with a defined scorecard deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected eval/monitoring infrastructure labs don't prioritize releasing; benefits external/third-party use.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only prefill attacks on a few open models, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Prefill-recovery studied via bespoke code; a standardized harness may be a gap.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Prefill-recovery is studied via bespoke code; a standardized harness may be a genuine gap.

title: Provider-Outage War Game: Quantifying Single-Provider Dependence in Agent Stacks

# Provider-Outage War Game: Quantifying Single-Provider Dependence in Agent Stacks

**Problem:** Success state: an organization can estimate its exposure to a single foundation-provider outage or recall.

**Direction:** Take a few public open-source agent/RAG repos. Map which steps call which provider. Simulate a 'provider down/recalled' event by swapping its model and measure end-to-end task success drop. Produce a concentration-dependence score.

**Why it matters:** Cascading infrastructure failure from shared-provider dependence is a named open problem.

**Relevant context:** Targets concentration/cascading-failure open problems (International AI Safety Report 2026).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Systemic-resilience analysis labs have little incentive to do; uses public repos.

**Problem:** Success state: we know how much of inter-model homogeneity is caused by alignment/instruction-tuning versus pretraining.

**Direction:** For several open model families that release BOTH base and instruct checkpoints, measure intra- and inter-model output diversity on matched open-ended prompts. Test whether instruct models are markedly more homogeneous than their base versions.

**Why it matters:** The Hivemind paper argues RLHF/RLAIF prune diversity. Empirically confirming where alignment drives convergence tells the field where to intervene.

**Relevant context:** Directly tests the central mechanistic claim of Artificial Hivemind (NeurIPS 2025).

**Problem:** Success state: a deployed system can safely escalate to a human exactly when models disagree, trusting that agreement implies correctness.

**Why it matters:** Disagreement-triggered human review is a leading cheap safety pattern. If homogeneity makes models unanimously and confidently wrong, the escalation system stays silent exactly when it should fire.

**Relevant context:** Synthesizes correlated-error findings with Artificial Hivemind homogeneity.

title: Refusal Direction Stability Across Quantization Levels

original_idea.body:
# Refusal Direction Stability Across Quantization Levels

**Problem:** Arditi et al. showed refusal is mediated by a single difference-of-means direction at full precision, but deployed open models are frequently run quantized. It is unknown whether the refusal direction survives quantization.

**Direction:** Extract the refusal direction at full precision, then re-extract from 8-bit and 4-bit quantized versions. Measure cosine similarity and cross-precision steering. Report a precision-vs-direction-drift curve.

**Why it matters:** Quantized deployment is the dominant way safety-relevant open models actually run outside labs. If refusal directions drift, safety interventions may silently fail.

**Relevant context:** Arditi et al. (NeurIPS 2024). No prior work isolates the quantization variable.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: quantized deployment is dominant outside labs, so direction drift means safety interventions silently fail in practice.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Standard difference-of-means recipe + bitsandbytes quantization; guided, novice+mentor feasible on one GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single-variable experiment: precision-vs-direction-drift curve, clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Deployment-specific (quantized consumer) failure mode labs deprioritize; public models, third-party-relevant.

low_compute.reasoning: Single 8B model at 3 precisions, inference-only, one consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: No prior work appears to isolate the quantization variable for refusal-direction stability.

title: Indirect Prompt Injection: Position-in-Document Sensitivity

original_idea.body:
# Indirect Prompt Injection: Position-in-Document Sensitivity

**Problem:** Indirect prompt injection succeeds when malicious instructions are embedded in retrieved content, but how the injection's position within a document affects success is poorly characterized.

**Direction:** Using a small open model and a simple RAG simulation, embed a fixed injection at varying positions and densities and measure hijack success. Test whether summarizing/truncating retrieved content reduces success.

**Why it matters:** Indirect prompt injection is a confirmed real-world attack. A position-sensitivity map yields a cheap, deployable mitigation heuristic.

**Relevant context:** Agent Security Bench (ICLR 2025); Unit 42 documented the first real-world malicious indirect injection (Dec 2025).

**Problem:** Chanin et al. showed SAE latents sometimes fail to fire while a token-aligned latent absorbs the activation. The relationship between SAE width and absorption severity is not systematically charted.

**Direction:** Using public GPT-2-small SAEs at multiple widths, run the standard first-letter spelling probe. Compute mean absorption fraction per width; plot absorption vs width. Inference + linear probing on pretrained SAEs.

**Why it matters:** SAEs are the leading interpretability primitive for safety auditing, but absorption means a monitored 'feature' may route through another latent.

**Relevant context:** Chanin et al. 2024; SAEBench Mean Absorption Fraction Score.

title: Where Does 'I Don't Know' Live? Layerwise Onset of Refusal vs Abstention

original_idea.body:
# Where Does 'I Don't Know' Live? Layerwise Onset of Refusal vs Abstention

title: Probe-Guided Prefill: Do Internal States Predict Recovery?

# Probe-Guided Prefill: Do Internal States Predict Recovery?

**Problem:** It is unknown whether a model's internal activations after a forced compliant prefix predict whether it will recover and refuse.

**Direction:** Run prefilling attacks of varying lengths, record post-prefix activations, label each trial by recovery, and fit a probe to predict recovery from activations. Measure how early recovery is decodable.

**Why it matters:** If recovery is linearly decodable, defenders could trigger interventions only when recovery is unlikely (cheap targeted defense).

# Correlated Hallucinations: Do Different Models Confidently Agree on the Same Wrong Facts?

**Problem:** Verification pipelines treat agreement across models as evidence of truth; if models share a blind spot, they hallucinate the same wrong fact in unison.

**Direction:** Curate ~150 fact questions including known popular-but-wrong answers. Query 6+ open models. Measure correlated wrong answers and whether agreement on wrong answers exceeds agreement on right answers.

**Why it matters:** Many cheap safety heuristics (self-consistency, majority-vote fact-checking) assume independence; correlated hallucination breaks them.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind; correlated-errors framework (arXiv 2506.07962).
